findings.description: Duplicate supplier URLs reused one candidate primary key.
findings.failure_scenario: The stored-image and scraper suppliers return the same product URL -> both audit rows receive one UUID -> the batch insert fails and every finalist loses origin qualification.

findings.description: The removal migration deleted evidence objects instead of enforcing the empty-bucket precondition.
findings.failure_scenario: The production bucket unexpectedly contains an object -> deployment silently destroys evidence even though the accepted plan authorizes dropping only an empty bucket.

findings.description: The trail fixture selected the first returned sibling instead of the qualified target.
findings.failure_scenario: PostgREST returns the two inserted sibling products in a different order -> the unqualified sibling is placed on the trail -> the qualified-product journey fails nondeterministically.

findings.description: Off-host audit candidates could consume the 25-candidate ceiling before official pages.
findings.failure_scenario: Google image provenance supplies 25 marketplace URLs with better positions and the scraper supplies official product pages -> slicing before host priority removes every official page and the products phase publishes nothing.

findings.description: Retired verification query state survived ordinary filter updates and stale SEO/cache contracts.
findings.failure_scenario: A visitor opens a legacy verification-filter URL and changes another facet -> the retired parameter remains in the URL and disagrees with the parser, canonical, and cache vocabulary.

findings.description: An unrelated DeepSeek service was accidentally activated while restoring the MIT registry entry.
findings.failure_scenario: Operational inventory consumers read the branch -> a dormant provider appears as an active production dependency, creating a false health and ownership signal.

findings.description: The new cron route returned a 500 without reporting the exception to error tracking.
findings.failure_scenario: A registry download or database write fails in production -> the cron caller sees 500 but Sentry receives no exception, delaying detection beyond the weekly freshness budget.
